eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and other models indicate a maximum temperature in Tokyo on August 13 centering on 28–29°C, driven by a mix of summer monsoon moisture, scattered thunderstorms, and variable cloud cover that limits peak solar heating. With market-implied probabilities tightly clustered around 27–29°C, traders are weighing short-term model runs showing modest instability against the broader subtropical high-pressure influence typical for mid-August, where small shifts in steering patterns or precipitation timing can alter outcomes by 1–2°C.

Recent model guidance from sources such as the Met Office and regional monitoring indicates a daytime maximum near 29–30°C, with overnight lows around 22–24°C, consistent with seasonal August averages of ~30°C highs that have been trending slightly lower mid-month due to decreasing solar angles and increasing monsoon influences. Thunderstorms and moderate rain expected on the 13th are key cooling factors, limiting peak insolation, promoting evaporative cooling, and introducing cloud cover that reduces surface heating compared to clearer, hotter days earlier in the week.

These conditions align with historical late-summer patterns in Beijing, where convective activity often caps temperatures below heatwave thresholds (>35°C, now less likely). Market-implied odds emphasize this narrow band because ensemble forecasts show limited day-to-day variability, with only modest upside risk if storms weaken or winds shift southerly. eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent high-pressure ridging over the southern Plains has maintained hot, dry conditions across Central Texas, with National Weather Service forecasts calling for a high near 101°F in Austin on August 13 amid mostly sunny skies and light southerly winds. This setup aligns with the market-implied odds favoring 100-101°F as the most likely outcome, reflecting model consensus on limited moisture and modest mixing that caps daytime maxima around the seasonal average. Recent upper-air analyses show the ridge holding steady without significant weakening or tropical moisture intrusion expected through the period, though small forecast adjustments in boundary-layer humidity could shift the peak by a degree or two. Historical August data indicate similar synoptic patterns typically produce highs in the upper 90s to low 100s, supporting trader positioning around these thresholds ahead of final observations.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Masroor Airbase Station in degrees Celsius on 14 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent short-term forecasts for Karachi point to a daily high near 31–32°C on August 14 amid typical southwest monsoon conditions, with extensive cloud cover, high humidity, and scattered showers or thunderstorms expected to limit daytime heating. Model guidance from sources such as AccuWeather and Pakistan Meteorological Department aligns with long-term August climatology, where average highs reach about 31–32°C (88–90°F) under similar moisture-laden regimes, rarely exceeding 33–34°C without clear skies. Any breaks in cloud or delayed precipitation could push readings toward the upper end of that range, while heavier rain would favor the lower side; traders have assigned roughly 94% combined probability to 31–33°C outcomes, reflecting this narrow band of likely maximum temperatures two days ahead. Updated model runs and official briefings over the next 24–48 hours will refine the exact peak.
